rows.title: Is Colorado’s cost of living higher than the national average?
rows.standfirst: Yes. The minimum income that Colorado residents need to afford basic necessities is among the highest in the nation.

rows.title: Colorado’s AI compromise would drop requirement that companies explain how their technology works
rows.standfirst: Companies that create and use artificial intelligence wouldn’t have to disclose how their systems help make decisions on things like hiring, loans and housing under a bill introduced Friday in the Colorado Senate. But the long-awaited measure tweaking Colorado’s first-in-the-nation law regulating AI would still require companies and other organizations using AI to notify consumers […]

rows.title: What’s Working: 44 years after Colorado’s Black Sunday, an incubator in Grand Junction keeps businesses running
rows.standfirst: Of the nearly 2,300 businesses launched, 86% are still in business after five years, says the Business Incubator Center in Grand Junction. Plus: Colorado jobs, inflation and more!

rows.title: Nexstar Tegna antitrust lawsuit now bipartisan, Nexstar fires back
rows.standfirst: Five new states sign on to the attempt to derail the $6.1B deal, three are from states with Republican attorneys general

rows.title: Colorado state lawmakers abandon efforts to legalize smaller lots for single-family homes
rows.standfirst: The Senate’s Local Government and Housing Committee voted in April to kill the proposals amid fierce resistance from local officials and some neighborhood groups

rows.title: As Colorado gas prices near $4.50 per gallon, driving to work is like taking a pay cut
rows.standfirst: It’s even more painful for truckers and ride-sharing drivers. Many are contractors who are paying out of pocket to fuel up.

rows.title: CNN founder Ted Turner, a brash and outspoken television pioneer, has died at age 87
rows.standfirst: Brash, outspoken television pioneer raced yachts, owned huge chunks of the American West and transformed the news business by launching CNN.

rows.title: Colorado’s labor force shrinks again in March to fourth-lowest participation rate since 1976
rows.standfirst: The state’s unemployment rate remains at 3.9%. Fewer are unemployed and employed, which is impacting the size of Colorado’s labor force.

rows.title: Colorado bill exempting sales tax from credit card swipe fees advances to governor after big Capitol showdown
rows.standfirst: Bill to exempt sales taxes from swipe fees heads to Gov. Jared Polis as industry warns of legal fights and consumer impacts

rows.title: Colorado’s wolf reintroduction hits “inflection point” as program leader steps down, population dwindles and conflicts increase
rows.standfirst: Eric Odell, Colorado Parks and Wildlife’s wolf conservation program manager since the program’s inception, announces his retirement

rows.title: Nearly half of Coloradans experiencing food insecurity don’t qualify for SNAP
rows.standfirst: Hundreds of thousands of Coloradans who make too much to qualify for food benefits still struggle to get enough to eat.

rows.title: What’s Working: Swipe fees, AI and other legislation Colorado businesses are cheering or fearing
rows.standfirst: A more collaborative year for businesses. Plus: A new moon rover, drought tech and new law could help CenturyLink end copper wire theft

rows.title: Rumors of ruined Western Slope peach crop were greatly exaggerated, growers say
rows.standfirst: A cold snap did destroy the peaches in North Fork Valley orchards, but the remaining 80-90% of the crop will start hitting fruit stands in June — much earlier than normal

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers reject environmentalist-backed effort to regulate data centers
rows.standfirst: Sponsors added a tax incentive but it was not enough to get the bill passed

rows.title: Colorado’s fierce two-year fight over AI regulation ends with watered-down law, little fanfare
rows.standfirst: Companies, governments and other groups that create and use artificial intelligence will no longer have to disclose how their AI systems help make decisions on things like hiring, loans and housing

rows.title: Bill reauthorizing Public Utilities Commission races through state Capitol. The story is what’s not included.
rows.standfirst: Xcel, Black Hills, some businesses backed failed attempts to amend the bill to grow the commission to 5 members in the interest of “ideological diversity”

rows.title: Democrats abandon rollback of business tax breaks to fund family tax credit after Colorado governor’s veto threat
rows.standfirst: House Bills 1221 and 1222 were killed in the Senate Finance Committee on Monday at their sponsors’ request in response to a veto threat from Gov. Jared Polis

rows.title: 101 bills that passed and failed in Colorado’s legislature this year that you need to know about
rows.standfirst: The Colorado Sun and Colorado Capitol News Alliance parsed through nearly 650 pieces of legislation debated in the legislature this year to find the ones that will most directly impact people’s lives — or would have had they passed

rows.title: Watch: Basic income programs in Denver and beyond at Colorado SunFest 2026
rows.standfirst: During Colorado SunFest 2026, panelists explored the feasibility, considerations and impacts of these interventions. It draws in part on panelist research and evidence from the Denver Basic Income Project, one such intervention targeting homelessness.

rows.title: What’s Working: Distributors trade tips on artificial intelligence during Denver event
rows.standfirst: Few have seen a return on their AI investments. It’s still early, trade group says. Plus: New quantum-computing lab in Boulder, small business certification program and Grand Lake’s new makerspace.

rows.title: If this is sad, we don’t want to be happy: An ice cream story
rows.standfirst: Denver’s Sadboy Creamery makes scarcity a virtue while it simultaneously charms and annoys Flavortown. And it’s the best ice cream this reporter has ever had.

rows.title: Northeastern Colorado has a lot to brag about, but also big socioeconomic challenges that will take many hands to solve
rows.standfirst: Community gathered to talk through new research on the 6-county region and concluded fixing the problems will require reaching across county lines

rows.title: More than 1,700 Cargill union workers shut out from job a day after rejecting contract
rows.standfirst: Members were told to stay home with pay for the past four weeks as negotiations continued. Pay ended last night.

rows.title: 3 Colorado quantum-computing makers swap some equity for $100 million each in federal funding
rows.standfirst: Atom Computing, Infleqtion and Quantinuum plan to speed up their efforts to scale production of quantum computers.

rows.title: What’s Working: Front Range foreclosures are on the rise
rows.standfirst: So are calls to the state’s foreclosure hotline. Plus: Colorado added jobs in April, state awards $7.5 million in grants to innovative startups and research and more!

rows.title: When thrifting isn’t thrifty: A look at the market trends making secondhand buying unaffordable
rows.standfirst: Thrift shops may be mission-driven, but they have bills to pay, too, that are helping drive up the cost of clothing and homegoods

rows.title: Oil and gas companies drilled and polluted less in 2025, but emissions from each well are rising, Colorado regulators say
rows.standfirst: Water is also a worry, with producers recycling a far lower percentage than in 2023, led by Western Slope and Front Range operations

rows.title: Colorado lunar rover picked by NASA to provide transport for Artemis moon missions
rows.standfirst: Lunar Outpost’s Pegasus LTV seats two astronauts and can livestream from the moon’s surface. It’s the newest rover from the Golden-based company.

rows.title: Cotter Corp claims it is running out of money and can’t post a bond to assure uranium mill cleanup in Cañon City
rows.standfirst: In the meantime, EPA proposes “targeted cleanup,” moving contaminated soils into impoundments where 5.3M tons of radioactive waste is buried

rows.title: Colorado overhauls state IT office, lays off 173 employees after negative feedback
rows.standfirst: The agency handles the tech behind the scenes for many state agencies, but dismal customer-satisfaction surveys and complaints have spurred drastic change.

rows.title: What’s Working: Saving Jamestown’s historic Mercantile, where everybody knows your name
rows.standfirst: Keeping the Merc local, with the help of some friends. Plus: Colorado’s average wages, quantum growth, 1,600 new houses for Aurora, and more!
